value.body: An aquaculture technician looks after fish or shrimp farms. They check water quality, plan feeding, watch for disease and help with harvests. Employers include fish and shrimp farms, feed and aqua-health companies, and government and NGO farming projects.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.F.Sc (some employers also take related science graduates)

items.label: Where you work
items.value: Fish and shrimp farms, mostly in coastal and rural districts

items.label: Seafood exports
items.note: Worth about ₹62,400 crore (US$ 7.45 billion) in FY 2024-25

items.label: Frozen shrimp's share of seafood exports
items.note: About 7.4 lakh tonnes of frozen shrimp in FY 2024-25

items.label: Inland share of fish output
items.note: Inland fisheries and aquaculture against ~44 lakh tonnes from the sea
items.source: Department of Fisheries data, as reported

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a farm, feed company or aqua-health company as a trainee or technical executive, often with field postings. Hatchery or farm internships during the degree help.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Spotting and reporting fish or shrimp disease

value.title: At a glance
items: The job is field-based and often outside cities.
With experience it can lead to farm manager or technical service roles.
Some move into feed or health product sales, or start their own farm.

competition.note: B.F.Sc graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among B.F.Sc graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
